claims.text: As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi thin films or patterned nanoribbons possess pronounced heterogeneous strain fields.
Lithographic patterning and nanoscale dimensions induce heterogeneous strain fields in the FeMnNiGeSi material.
The heterogeneous strain fields promote local phase disparities.
Local phase disparities produce spatially varying magneto-thermal coupling during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Strain gradients induce spatially varying phase-transformation behavior.
Spatially inhomogeneous phase behavior affects magnetic-domain dynamics during applied-field cycles.
The proposed inhomogeneity diminishes the magnetocaloric response relative to bulk forms.
The proposed inhomogeneity increases hysteresis relative to bulk forms.
Controlled annealing below the onset of unwanted secondary phases can relax the strain fields without causing full phase homogenization.
Annealing-induced strain relaxation produces more uniform phase-transformation behavior.
Annealing-induced strain relaxation improves magnetocaloric performance.
Post-annealing samples will exhibit reduced magnetic hysteresis relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Post-annealing samples will exhibit a larger magnetocaloric temperature change relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Post-annealing behavior will trend closer to bulk-material behavior under similar conditions.
The proposed relationship is applicable specifically to nanoscale thin-film and nanoribbon geometries under low applied fields.
